kinds.name: People
kinds.what: a folder per person — PROFILE.md (who they are, their story, why they matter here) and WORKS.md

kinds.name: Groups
kinds.what: schools, movements, organizations, lineages

kinds.name: Periods
kinds.what: eras and events worth studying on their own

kinds.name: Works
kinds.what: buildings, books, artworks — studied as objects in themselves

kinds.name: Places
kinds.what: real locations

kinds.name: Concepts
kinds.what: ideas, principles and terms

kinds.name: Practices
kinds.what: techniques, methods, exercises — things you do (with a level when there is an order)

kinds.name: Systems
kinds.what: products, tools and implementations (technology topics)

kinds.name: Patterns
kinds.what: reusable designs (technology topics)

kinds.name: Resources
kinds.what: what you learn from — books, papers, courses, videos — each with its link and what it contributes

kinds.name: Sources
kinds.what: where information came from — reports, sites, documents — each with its link

kinds.name: Evidence
kinds.what: facts that support or challenge a claim, each tied to its source

kinds.name: Interviews
kinds.what: conversations with people, and what was learned from each

kinds.name: Data
kinds.what: numbers and datasets, and where they came from

kinds.name: Experiments
kinds.what: tests that were run — what was tried, how, and what happened

kinds.name: Results
kinds.what: what came out of the work — outcomes, findings, numbers

kinds.name: Options
kinds.what: the choices on the table, side by side

kinds.name: Plans
kinds.what: how something will get done — steps, order, who

kinds.name: Workstreams
kinds.what: parallel strands of the work, each with its own owner

kinds.name: Timeline
kinds.what: milestones and target dates

kinds.name: Responsibilities
kinds.what: who does each part, and who covers when they’re out — only what people have agreed to

kinds.name: Dependencies
kinds.what: what this needs from other people or systems, and what relies on it

kinds.name: Schedule
kinds.what: how often something happens, deadlines and the calendar

kinds.name: Research
kinds.what: what was looked into for this work (a folder type — not the Research kind of work)

kinds.name: Design
kinds.what: how it should look and work

kinds.name: Build
kinds.what: how it is being made, and what exists so far

kinds.name: Launch
kinds.what: getting it out — rollout, announcements, first use

kinds.name: Review
kinds.what: looking back — what happened against what was expected (a folder type — not reviewing in conversation)

kinds.name: Processes
kinds.what: how something is done, step by step — a page per process

kinds.name: Checklists
kinds.what: steps to run through each time

kinds.name: Runs
kinds.what: notes on a single run — only when something was unusual

kinds.name: Measures
kinds.what: what is watched, and the range that counts as normal

kinds.name: Incidents
kinds.what: when something went wrong — what happened, the fix, what changes

kinds.name: Improvements
kinds.what: changes worth trying to make it work better

studying.howILearn: Through conversation. You teach; I call out what resonates and we follow that thread; along the way you name the few things worth remembering, and they stick. When we stop, save it: update the pages it touched (what resonated, what to remember), add any idea of mine as a concept, and add a learning-path entry if the inquiry changed direction.

classifications.label: Decision
classifications.note: A decision was made, with the evidence behind it

classifications.label: Assumption
classifications.note: Taken as true, not yet tested

classifications.label: Known issue
classifications.note: A confirmed, stable problem or limitation

classifications.label: Method / how-to
classifications.note: How something should be done or analyzed

classifications.label: Fact from a source
classifications.note: A fact from a source — a spec sheet, a measurement, a document, a test result; without a source it is an assumption

classifications.label: Question / dispute
classifications.note: Someone questions a conclusion, number or record — still open ("are you sure?" counts)

classifications.label: Correction
classifications.note: An earlier statement was wrong; this replaces it. Fill supersedes: and mark the old record superseded

classifications.label: Interpretation
classifications.note: An interpretation or reasoning — not a sourced fact; list what it rests on in references: / source_refs:

classifications.label: Preference
classifications.note: How the owner wants output produced

neverSave: Passwords, API keys and other secrets
Personal medical records — diagnoses, test results, treatment
